persona: Simulated absolute beginner who likes relaxed lo-fi music

outcome.status: UI composition, save, WAV export and MIDI export completed; VST playback reliability blocked
outcome.description: Created an eight-note melody using the Rill Lab Sine VST3, combined it with the supplied drum audio, slowed the project to 96 BPM and duplicated both tracks to a displayed duration of 30.000 seconds. Named the project rain tea using the built-in mouse keyboard. The UI confirmed both exports. Playback reported plugin/render failures and stopped near the start after retry; no audio was auditioned.

rating_reasons.easy_to_use: The empty-track hint, Pencil, marquee selection and Duplicate let me build a short piece quickly. Opening an existing pattern was less obvious, and playback errors prevented confidence in the result.
rating_reasons.how_cool_it_looks: The restrained dark colors, clear waveforms, spacious arrangement and readable note blocks look polished and inviting.
rating_reasons.how_fast_it_is: Most edits appeared promptly and I made a sketch quickly. Native dialogs needed a moment to appear, WAV export needed a noticeable wait, and playback retry failed. This is a subjective score in the laboratory environment.
rating_reasons.how_confusing_it_is: The clip end and many editing tools were initially uncertain. Changing tempo left waveform space inside the audio box, and plugin errors did not explain a beginner-friendly repair.
rating_reasons.feature_completeness: Mouse drawing, a VST library, copying, naming, save and both export formats were available. Reliable instrument playback was not achieved in this session, so the requested end-to-end experience felt incomplete.

findings.observation: The empty arrangement hint opened the instrument library and Assign instrument created a MIDI track and pattern.
findings.recommendation: Keep this direct entry point and consider explicitly naming the next step for editing the new pattern.

findings.observation: Double-clicking the new pattern at its body produced no visible editor; right-clicking revealed Edit notes, which worked.
findings.recommendation: Make the existing-pattern edit gesture visible and consistent, or expose an Edit notes action when a pattern is selected.

findings.observation: Pencil and the note-length menu worked with the mouse, and drawing past the old clip end automatically lengthened the pattern.
findings.recommendation: Preserve automatic growth and add a short hint that notes can extend the clip.

findings.observation: Reducing tempo from 112 to 96 made the four-bar box 10 seconds, while the audio waveform ended earlier inside its box. I could not tell whether this meant stretching or a gap.
findings.recommendation: Explain whether an audio clip follows tempo, and provide a visible beginner-friendly tempo-follow or stretch control.

findings.observation: Marquee-selecting both tracks and choosing Duplicate made adjacent copies; the title clearly confirmed 30.000 seconds.
findings.recommendation: Keep the selected-clip count and visible total duration; consider a readily visible repeat action.

findings.observation: Playback displayed Plug-in/render error with 1758 failures. The suggested stop/restart then stopped near the beginning with Plugin processing failed on New instrument.
findings.recommendation: Identify the failing device and offer an actionable recovery path with clear status. Investigate the supplied lab VST failure without generalizing this session to all third-party plugins.

findings.observation: Rename project offered an on-screen Keyboard with Clear and letter buttons, allowing the mouse-only name rain tea. Native pickers reused that name for project, WAV and MIDI.
findings.recommendation: Retain mouse-accessible naming and default filenames, and make the on-screen keyboard equally easy to find in other name fields.

findings.observation: WAV export displayed the arrangement duration and an effect-tail option. MIDI and WAV both eventually displayed explicit Exported confirmations.
findings.recommendation: Keep duration and completion feedback visible, and preserve a recent-export status so another operation cannot obscure whether an export completed.

positives: Clear dark visual design and readable arrangement.
Direct empty-area MIDI creation and visible instrument assignment.
Easy mouse note drawing with selectable lengths and automatic clip growth.
Marquee selection and Duplicate worked across audio and MIDI together.
Built-in mouse keyboard enabled an original project name.
Visible duration, export progress and export success feedback.
limitations: This was an independent simulated beginner session, not a human participant study.
All app input used the supplied mouse driver; the on-screen keyboard was operated by clicking its buttons. No physical keyboard input, shortcuts, source inspection or direct project edits were used.
No capture was auditioned, so there are no claims about heard sound, mix quality or whether the musical style sounds convincingly lo-fi.
Only the supplied stock audio and native Rill Lab Sine VST3 were used; this does not establish compatibility with other third-party plugins.
Playback was observed in software graphics with the documented 60 ms virtual audio buffering and 1024-frame requests at 48 kHz; no physical hardware latency claims are made.
Project and export paths are those accepted through native file pickers. Their contents and actual duration remain for the coordinator to verify independently.
The arrangement is a simple repeated melody over stock drums, with no listening-based refinement.
